title: The Holiness of the Church
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The holiness of the church means that God’s people are set apart for Him in doctrine, worship, conduct, love, purity, and witness. The church belongs to the holy God and must not make peace with sin or worldliness.
summary: The holiness of the church means that God’s people are set apart for Him in doctrine, worship, conduct, love, purity, and witness. The church belongs to the holy God and must not make peace with sin or worldliness.
christFocus: Jesus Christ gave Himself to cleanse and sanctify His church. He does not merely forgive His people; He makes them a holy people who reflect His character.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The church is holy because it belongs to God. Holiness is not spiritual superiority or cold religious appearance; it is being set apart for the Lord and shaped by His truth.

Christ loved the church and gave Himself to cleanse her. The holiness of the church therefore flows from grace, not self-righteousness. The same Savior who forgives also purifies.

The church’s holiness includes doctrine, worship, relationships, sexuality, speech, justice, mercy, and mission. God’s people cannot separate public worship from daily obedience.

Holiness also affects witness. A church that excuses sin while claiming Christ confuses the world and harms its members. A holy church displays the beauty and seriousness of belonging to God.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some churches become careless with sin in the name of grace, while others become harsh and self-righteous in the name of holiness. Scripture gives a better path: holy love rooted in Christ’s cleansing work.

This doctrine matters because Christ’s people are called to be distinct without becoming proud, pure without becoming merciless, and gracious without becoming compromised.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Pursue holiness as one cleansed by Christ, not as one trying to earn His love. Confess sin, reject compromise, receive correction, and help your church become a people marked by truth, purity, mercy, and worship before the Lord.
